skill_title: Analyse trends and critique misleading graphs
notes: 20-item bank. CAPS mix: 10 L3 / 10 L4. Identify trends, predict cautiously, spot truncated axes / distorted scales / cherry-picked ranges.

stimulus.inline: Line graph: sales rose Y1 100 → Y2 110 → Y3 121 → Y4 133.
Same series rising ~10% per year. Predict Y5.
Misleading: a chart truncates y-axis to start at 95 (not 0), making small differences look huge.
3D pie chart with one slice tilted forward, making it look bigger.
Cherry-picked range. 10-year data shows downward trend, but the chart only shows last 2 years (rising).

items.question: Issue?
options: Cherry-picked time range hides longer trend
items.expectedAnswer: Cherry-picked time range hides longer trend

stimulus.inline: Sales seasonal: hotter summer months higher. Predict next summer?
Inconsistent x-axis spacing (years 2010, 2012, 2015, 2020 with equal gaps).

items.question: Issue?
options: Unequal time gaps drawn equally — distorts trend
items.expectedAnswer: Unequal time gaps drawn equally — distorts trend

stimulus.inline: Bar chart with different bar widths (wide for highlighted bar).

items.question: Issue?
options: Different widths exaggerate the wider bar's value
items.expectedAnswer: Different widths exaggerate the wider bar's value
workingSteps: All bars must be same width.

stimulus.inline: Predict cautiously. Five years of rising sales doesn't guarantee future rise.

items.question: Best statement?
options: Sales will definitely keep rising at same rate.
Past trend continued, but external factors could change this.
items.expectedAnswer: Past trend continued, but external factors could change this.
workingSteps: Trends are not guarantees — caveat predictions.

stimulus.inline: Pictogram: 1 stick figure = 100 people. Chart shows 3 figures for boys and 5 for girls.
Misleading pictogram. Bigger figures used for higher categories, scaling area not number.

items.question: Issue?
options: Area scaling exaggerates difference (doubling height → 4× area)
items.expectedAnswer: Area scaling exaggerates difference (doubling height → 4× area)

stimulus.inline: Election poll chart shows 49% support truncated, 51% opposition shown as DOUBLE the bar height.

items.question: Issue?
options: Truncated axis and distortion misleads — 49 vs 51 not 'double'
items.expectedAnswer: Truncated axis and distortion misleads — 49 vs 51 not 'double'

stimulus.inline: Line graph: COVID-19 cases rose sharply in March 2020 then declined. Total at 12 months.

items.question: Predict 24 months?
options: Will follow a cycle (waves) — predict cautiously, not linearly
items.expectedAnswer: Will follow a cycle (waves) — predict cautiously, not linearly
workingSteps: Pandemic data is volatile — cycles, not a smooth trend.

stimulus.inline: Bar chart of rainfall (mm) where the y-axis goes from 80 mm to 110 mm only.
Two different scales on the same chart (left y for cases, right y for hospitalisations) — both lines look similar despite very different magnitudes.

items.question: Issue?
options: Two y-axes can make unrelated trends look related
items.expectedAnswer: Two y-axes can make unrelated trends look related

stimulus.inline: Predict from 5-year trend rising 8%/yr. Initial Y0 = R10 000. Predict Y5.
Pie chart slices don't sum to 100% (sums to 95%).

items.question: Issue?
options: Slices should sum to 100% — data missing or error
items.expectedAnswer: Slices should sum to 100% — data missing or error
workingSteps: A complete pie must sum to 100%.

stimulus.inline: 5-year sales graph shows clear upward trend. Sales fall 30% in Y6 (unexpected).

items.question: What does this teach about predictions?
options: Past trends are useful but not guaranteed — external shocks can occur.
items.expectedAnswer: Past trends are useful but not guaranteed — external shocks can occur.

stimulus.inline: Linear forecast: Y1 100, Y2 110, Y3 120. Predict Y10.
Same data. Compound model: rate 10% per year. Y10?

_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_PREDICTION: Treats past trend as guaranteed; over-/under-predicts.
